issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: char helpers for common ASCII categories
issue_context.body:
### Background and motivation

We have a bunch of IsHex/IsHexChar/IsHexDigit helpers all around our libraries, as well as IsAsciiLetter/IsAsciiLetterOrDigit and such variants.  We should expose these simple helpers implemented efficiently in a place all code can use rather than duplicating them into a bunch of libraries.  We already have many `Is*` methods on char, like `IsAscii`, `IsLetter`, `IsDigit`, and so on; we can augment those with the additional methods.

### API Proposal

```diff
public struct Char
{
+    public static bool IsAsciiDigit(char c); // true iff the char is 0-9
+    public static bool IsAsciiLetter(char c); // true iff the char is A-Z, a-z
+    public static bool IsAsciiLetterLower(char c); // true iff the char is a-z
+    public static bool IsAsciiLetterUpper(char c); // true iff the char is A-Z
+    public static bool IsAsciiLetterOrDigit(char c); // true iff the char is A-Z, a-z, 0-9

+    public static bool IsHexDigit(char c); // true iff the char is 0-9, A-F, a-f
+    public static bool IsHexDigitUpper(char c); // true iff the char is 0-9, A-F
+    public static bool IsHexDigitLower(char c); // true iff the char is 0-9, a-f

+    public static bool IsInRange(char c, char minInclusive, char maxInclusive); // true iff the char is >= minInclusive && <= maxInclusive
}
```

### API Usage

```C#
if (char.IsAsciiLetterOrDigit(c))
{
    writer.Write(c);
}
else
{
    writer.Write($@"\u{(int)c:X4}");
}
```

### Alternative Designs

We might also want to expose a helper for getting the value of a hex digit, e.g.
```C#
public static int GetHexDigitValue(char c); // return 0-15 for 0-9/A-F, and some sentinel otherwise (e.g. -1)
```

### Risks

_No response_

> public static bool IsHexDigit(char c, out )

This seems like it has an extra `out`. Should that just be `IsHexDigit(char c)`?

> This seems like it has an extra out. Should that just be IsHexDigit(char c)?

Yes, that was a copy/paste/delete error.

Thoughts on including this one in the list?
```c#
public static bool IsAsciiDigit(char c); // true iff the char is 0-9
```
Are non ASCII digits ever used in Hex representations?

> Are non ASCII digits ever used in Hex representations?

Not to my knowledge.

> public static bool IsAsciiDigit(char c); // true iff the char is 0-9

Added
Would it make sense to add these methods to other types? There are some existing `Is*` methods for `byte` and `int` in the framework and adding them to `Rune` is good for symmetry's sake.

> Would it make sense to add these methods to other types? There are some existing Is* methods for byte and int in the framework and adding them to Rune is good for symmetry's sake.

Adding to Rune as well seems reasonable.  We shouldn't add these to Byte or Int32.

This is appx what this would look like in dotnet/runtime:
https://github.com/stephentoub/runtime/commit/0146ecf5a5b3573e77a68bb7da496047acdd3f28

Getting rid of all this redundancy is awesome. @stephentoub according to your commit, these patterns show up everywhere. 👍 

How did you find and fix all those? Resharper structural search?

Well, then I can recommend structural search. You search for `$1 >= 'a' && $1 <= 'z'` and can replace it with a pattern (`char.IsXxx($1)`). I guess that could find a few more instances. This search is not so sensitive to the concrete syntax being used. It matches based on the C# syntax tree.
If you see more that can be changed, please let me know. The ones I'm aware of and didn't change are in projects that have at least one target below .NET 7.

[Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mhdY64EnxAw&t=0h0m0s)

* We inserted "Ascii" in the Is*Hex methods
* We renamed IsInRange to IsBetween
* Otherwise looks good

```C#
namespace System
{
    public partial struct Char
    {
        public static bool IsAsciiDigit(char c); // true iff the char is 0-9
        public static bool IsAsciiLetter(char c); // true iff the char is A-Z, a-z
        public static bool IsAsciiLetterLower(char c); // true iff the char is a-z
        public static bool IsAsciiLetterUpper(char c); // true iff the char is A-Z
        public static bool IsAsciiLetterOrDigit(char c); // true iff the char is A-Z, a-z, 0-9

        public static bool IsAsciiHexDigit(char c); // true iff the char is 0-9, A-F, a-f
        public static bool IsAsciiHexDigitUpper(char c); // true iff the char is 0-9, A-F
        public static bool IsAsciiHexDigitLower(char c); // true iff the char is 0-9, a-f

        public static bool IsBetween(char c, char minInclusive, char maxInclusive); // true iff the char is >= minInclusive && <= maxInclusive
    }
}
```
What's the state of the implementation for this? If it hasn't been tackled yet I could probably take a look at it.

Thanks, @dakersnar. It's basically done (commit mentioned a few comments back), I just need to polish it / adapt to the decisions in the meeting. I typically implement or at least protoptype proposals I make to fully flesh them out prior to spending time reviewing something, to help make sure we're reviewing the right thing :-)
@stephentoub you might also consider adding IsBase64 methods as well.

review_comments: Can this use the new API, or is it too low level to be dependent on it?
Unfortunately this file is compiled into a library that has a pre-.NET 7 target.  It wasn't worth ifdef'ing it to use the new API in some builds and the open-coded version in others.
Nice :)

Suggest changing this to say that the behavior is undefined if _minInclusive_ \> _maxInclusive_. We don't want to tie ourselves to an implementation such that we guarantee a specific behavior in the face of bad input, even though it's unlikely the implementation will ever change.
Steve - didn't you have some awesome bitmask you used in the Regex code for this? Wonder why we'd be using different code here vs. Regex?

That's based on https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/af2a48ddaec9a3e27002b0d3b80c07431c2e38c1/src/libraries/Common/src/System/HexConverter.cs#L337-L341, but it only works when the whole range is >= 64 (so that it can fit in a ulong), and here it would need to be more than that.

Isn't IsAsciiLetterUpper redundant with... uh... the rest of that?

Maybe it's an intentional short-circuit?
I assume it's a short-circuit.  Didn't want to dive in to optimizing this as that would be a giant hole :)

Open question: is `((uint)(c - 'A') & ~0x20u) < 26` a more effiicent pattern because it allows folding the MOV and SUB into a single LEA operation? (I don't know the answer to this re: perf, but it is a codegen size savings on x86.)

(Tanner seemed to think it should be left as-is for readability. I'd defer to his expertise in the absence of supporting evidence otherwise.)
Do you have a sharplab example that shows the lea?  I don't see a codegen size difference on x86, but I might be doing it wrong.

```cs
using System;

foreach (Char ch in "Hello!")
{
    if (IsAsciiLetter1(ch)) Console.WriteLine(ch);
}

foreach (Char ch in "Hello!")
{
    if (IsAsciiLetter2(ch)) Console.WriteLine(ch);
}

static bool IsAsciiLetter1(char c) => (uint)((c | 0x20) - 'a') <= 'z' - 'a';
static bool IsAsciiLetter2(char c) => (uint)((c - 'A') & ~0x20) < 26;
```

Suggest removing this test case and the test case two lines below. We shouldn't guarantee any specific behavior when the min \& max inputs are bad, since it locks us in to potentially unwanted behavior forevermore.

I'll update the XML comments to remove the guarantee, but I'll leave the test case; even if we don't guarantee the behavior, we should still be notified if we accidentally change it, as I expect someone somewhere will take a dependency on it.
I assume there's no concern for the output of this to be an older runtime where these members aren't available.
Unless someone created a frankenbuild with System.Text.RegularExpressions from .NET 7 and tried to use it with a pre-.NET 7 runtime, no.

?
```suggestion
        public static bool IsAsciiLetterOrDigit(char c) => IsAsciiLetter(c) || IsBetween(c, '0', '9');
```
This was on purpose in order to make it branch-free, since I don't know which inputs are going to be more common.

Consider replacing all of these `IsBetween(c, '0', '9')`s with `IsAsciiDigit(c)`.

I'll accept any sort of "no", from "I'm too lazy" to "it's important to not overwhelm the poor, overworked JIT inlining evaluator in these routines"
I was concerned about "the poor, overworked JIT" part of it and thus left them untouched.  If Levi says I should change them, though, I'm happy to.
I have no thoughts one way or another. Worry about the JIT is in the hands of more knowledgeable people. 🙂
